title: Local-LLM runtimes ship in-model speculative decoding on by default by Q2 2027
body: Ollama 0.31, released July 1, turned on multi-token prediction for Gemma 4 on Apple Silicon by default: the model ships a small draft that proposes several tokens, the main model verifies them in one pass and keeps what it agrees with, and Ollama measured Gemma 4 generating nearly 90% faster on a coding-agent benchmark with byte-identical output. Crucially this is a default, not a tuning flag, and the small-batch MLX matmul kernel Ollama upstreamed is usable by any MLX model rather than just Gemma. The mechanism is the sort of change that spreads across a runtime field once one shipping implementation proves the accuracy-neutral speedup: draft-model speculative decoding has existed as an opt-in in llama.cpp, vLLM, and MLX-LM for a while, but wiring it on out of the box, with a bundled draft and a working kernel, is what converts a benchmark into a default users never touch. Coding agents make the payoff structural because they call the model continuously over highly predictable text, so accepted drafts compound over a session. Expect a second mainstream local runtime shipping to end users, LM Studio, llama.cpp-based desktops, MLX-LM, or vLLM's local mode, to make in-model or paired-draft speculative decoding the default path for at least one popular open-weight model family rather than an advanced setting, closing more of the on-device-to-hosted throughput gap without new silicon.

reasoning.because: Ollama 0.31 shipped Gemma 4 MTP on by default, ~90% faster on coding agents, output unchanged
reasoning.given: Speculative decoding ships as opt-in in rival runtimes; accuracy-neutral wins spread once defaulted
reasoning.so_that: A second mainstream local runtime defaults speculative decoding on for a popular open-weight model family
reasoning.landing: by Q2 2027; a second end-user runtime's release notes flip it to on-by-default
reasoning.plain_language: Ollama made a local model run much faster for free by guessing several words ahead, so other apps will soon do the same by default.

summary: Ollama 0.31 turned multi-token prediction on by default for Gemma 4 on Apple Silicon, generating ~90% faster with identical output. Since draft-model speculative decoding is already opt-in elsewhere, expect a second mainstream local runtime to default it on for a popular open family by Q2 2027.
